newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkey to tender 200,000 T milling wheat Dec 10.
newsitem.headline: Turkey to tender 200,000 T milling wheat Dec 10.

text.p: Turkey's state grain board (TMO) will invite bids on December 10 in a tender to import 200,000 tonnes of red and white milling wheat on a three-year credit basis, a grain official said on Friday.
He said the imports would be made from either the United States, Australia, Argentina or any European Union member country.
"Up to 50,000 tonnes of the import will be for white milling wheat and the remaining for red wheat," said the official, who declined to be named.
"The wheat origin preferences are the United States, Canada, Argentina, Australia and any member of the European Union," he told Reuters.
"The import will be made on a three-year credit basis, in prices given in FOB or C+F," he said.
He said the tender announcements would be made on national newspapers on Monday, when other details could be known.
The open tender will be held at 0800 GMT on December 10 at the TMO head office in Ankara, he said.
The official did not say when the deliveries would be.
A Swiss-based trader said three-year maturity was a long-term credit and only governments can finance such a trade.
"I believe the import terms on credit can only be met by the United States," he said.

The TMO has been considering wheat imports and was authorised by the government to buy up to 500,000 tonnes to moderate local wheat prices which have gone up 30 percent since Turkey cracked down on imports from the United States for inspections against crop disease last month. --Ercan Ersoy, Ankara Newsroom, 90-312-4462940
